subject: GPU availability & soft-lock request — OmegaSprint (late-stage)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU availability check + soft-lock request for OmegaSprint

Team —

OmegaSprint (late-stage, expected commit this quarter) just signaled intent to reserve dedicated capacity for a 3-month pilot with a possible scale to sustained reserves. They asked us to hold capacity while procurement finalizes terms. Can we do an immediate availability check and place a 72-hour soft-lock on the nodes that match their profile?

Key details they provided:
- Workload: fine-tuning + high-concurrency inferencing (mixed training-ish jobs, mostly long sequence generation)
- Preferred model class: 70B family (quantized FP16/INT8 preferred), target ~40 tokens/sec sustained per GPU for benchmarks
- Volume: initial request ~6 GPUs (NVIDIA H100-class equivalence) with a 6–8 week ramp to 24 GPUs if POC performance looks good
- Desired start window: earliest 2029-07-08

Ask: Marcus / Infra — can you run quick capacity mapping and advise whether we have the nodes available in us-west and if a soft-lock is feasible? Marissa — will need the soft-lock ticket + wording for procurement (non-binding hold). Laura / Rishi — please weigh in on fallback model variants (smaller models we can route automatically) so we can include that in the playbook.

I want to move fast — Kevin from OmegaSprint is on standby for a short call. If we can place a soft-lock today it materially improves close probability.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU availability check + soft-lock request for OmegaSprint

Ben —

I can open a soft-lock ticket with ops right away. A couple of quick clarifying items that procurement will ask for so we can word the hold properly:
- Exact GPU spec you want us to hold (H100 equivalence vs specific SKU)
- Whether the hold is node-level or pool-level (node-level preferred for bookkeeping)
- Proposed expiry of soft-lock (72 hours is OK by default; we can set a later expiry if legal asks for an extension)

I'll draft the hold notice and attach it to the HubSpot deal. Marcus — if you can reply with the SKU mapping and a provisional hold id format I will create the ticket and copy Kevin.

Marissa Cole
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU availability check + soft-lock request for OmegaSprint

Ben / team —

Quick inventory snapshot attached (inventory_snapshot_20290625.csv). TL;DR: we have 18 H100-equivalent slots in us-west pool A that are currently unreserved across the 2029-07-08 window. 12 of those are associated with inf-quantized profiles (good for INT8/FP16 serving and faster kernel paths).

Notes and caveats:
- If OmegaSprint insists on single-tenant pinned nodes (no multi-tenancy), the usable count drops to 8 in us-west (due to maintenance scheduling and existing soft commitments).
- We can place a 72-hour soft-lock today. I'll reserve a tag HOLD-OMEGA-20290625-01 in the orchestration layer and mark the nodes in the pool. This is non-binding and will auto-expire unless extended by a formal reserve request.
- Fallback plan: we can route traffic to a quantized 30B variant we maintain if their tests show latency issues; this reduces per-GPU capacity but improves availability.

Attachment: inventory_snapshot_20290625.csv (CSV, 42 KB)

Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Capacity Lead | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Kevin Liao <kevin@omegasprint.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@omegasprint.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU availability check + soft-lock request for OmegaSprint

Ben —

Thanks for the run-down. Confirming: OmegaSprint intends to commit to an initial 3-month reserved pilot if we can secure nodes for our POC. We prefer H100-equivalent hardware. We are comfortable with a 72-hour soft-lock while procurement finalizes the MOA.

A couple of clarifying items from our side:
- We'll sign a short MOA (term sheet attached in a follow-up email) that has a conversion path to a full reserved contract if the POC meets throughput targets.
- Engineering note: we will start with 6 GPUs, run multi-instance fine-tuning workloads, and then expand to up to 24 GPUs over 6–8 weeks depending on the pilot.

Please go ahead with the soft-lock and let us know what you need from procurement. We can do a quick call this afternoon to align on next steps.

Best,
Kevin Liao
Director, Platform & ML Engineering
OmegaSprint Labs
kevin@omegasprint.com

Kevin —

Thanks, appreciate the quick confirmation. Marissa / Marcus — please place the 72-hour soft-lock (HOLD-OMEGA-20290625-01) on 6 H100-equivalent nodes in us-west pool A and attach the hold notice to HubSpot. Marissa — please copy Kevin and procurement on the hold notice.

Laura / Rishi — please prepare a short fallback playbook for the quantized 30B variant (latency, expected throughput, recommended routing policy) so we can include it in the MOA.

Kevin — once the soft-lock is in place I'll schedule a 30-minute call to walk procurement/legal through the MOA path and the conversion triggers. Looking forward to closing this.

Ben
